verdict: OK to lend in Indore auto & components, but only to tier-1/tier-2 suppliers with diversified OEM order books and tight monthly monitoring; avoid single-OEM, EV-powertrain-exposed and thin-margin job-work units.
title: Indore Auto & Auto Components: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What this business physically is
**Indore's auto cluster is component fabrication and sub-assembly feeding OEMs, plus a strong local vehicle-retail pull.** Inputs are steel, aluminium and bought-out castings; cash comes back only after the OEM approves the part, runs it through its line and pays on its cycle. **Value sits in the tooling and the approved-part relationship, not in the machine.** So when a proposal lands, check whether the borrower owns its dies and has a written schedule agreement; if the part is made to a single customer's drawing with no tooling ownership, ask who pays for the die and what happens on model change.

## Where cash and margin actually sit
**Pricing power is thin and passed through, so margin is made on operating efficiency, not price.** Peer results show the split: Motherson Sumi Wiring lifted net profit 35% to Rs 223 crore on revenue up 46.7% to Rs 4,054 crore [4], while ASK Automotive hit record revenue but aluminium squeezed margins [5]. **Working capital is the real loan.** Rating commentary puts gross current assets at 160-170 days [10], and flags Debt/EBITDA above 2.5-2.75 times as the stress line [10]. So when a proposal lands, check the receivable days against the named OEM's actual payment record; if receivables run past the stated OEM cycle, ask for the bank statement showing receipts, not the ledger.

## What has changed now
**National output is strong but credit is running ahead of it.** IIP for NIC 29 is +25.2% YoY and +19.2% Apr-to-date [D], yet bank credit is +27.0% YoY against that +19.2% output, a gap of +7.8 pp [D].

## Who to pursue, who to avoid
**Pursue tier-1 and tier-2 component makers with two or more OEM customers, owned tooling and EV-agnostic parts.** Lumax Auto raised its growth guidance on a strong first half [7], and ASK is winning EV components across braking and lightweighting [5] - that is the borrower profile to back. **Avoid single-OEM job-work units, engine-and-fuel-system specialists facing obsolescence [11], and anyone whose growth is funded by credit rather than orders.** If a proposal's sales growth outruns the OEM's own volume growth, ask for the purchase order book before sanction.

## How to grow safely
**Structure short, secure the receivables, and take numbers every month.** Keep tenor inside the OEM payment cycle, take hypothecation of receivables and a charge on tooling, and cap Debt/EBITDA at 2.5 times in covenant [10]. **Every month take the sales register, the top-customer receivable ageing and the GST return.** If receivable days stretch beyond the agreed OEM cycle for two months, cut the drawing power; if Debt/EBITDA crosses 2.5 times, stop fresh limits and review.
